Claude Design Is Quietly Replacing Figma (Here's The Full Breakdown)
Most people haven't realized this yet…
But the way we design is changing fast.
For years, tools like Figma and Canva required:
Manual layout work, constant tweaking, hours of effort.
Now, there's a new workflow:
Describe → Generate → Refine
That's exactly what Claude Design enables.
After testing it deeply, one thing is clear:
This isn't just another AI feature. It's a completely new way to create visuals.
What Claude Design Actually Does
Claude Design is a dedicated workspace where you collaborate with AI to create UI prototypes, slide decks, infographics, marketing assets, and one-pagers.
Everything is generated from natural language prompts. Instead of designing manually, you direct the system.
Section I — Getting Access (60 Seconds)
Open Claude on web and look at the left sidebar. You'll see a new option called "Design."
Claude Design (left sidebar)
Click it. You'll instantly enter a separate interface built specifically for visual creation.
Section II — Home Screen Overview
Once inside, your dashboard will look like this:
Claude Design home screen
This screen is your central hub where you can access recent projects, explore examples, use design systems, and start new work.
Understanding The Layout
Claude Design is split into two main areas:
Left Side — Chat Panel
This is where you describe what you want, iterate on outputs, and guide the AI.
Right Side — Canvas
This is your live preview area, workspace for outputs, and real-time editing zone.
Chat panel highlighted
Canvas highlighted
Left = thinking. Right = building.
Section III — Starting A Design
When you begin, you'll see four creation paths:
4 options (Prototype, Slide deck, Template, Other)
  1. Prototype — Used for interactive UI flows
  2. Slide Deck — For presentations
  3. From Template — Prebuilt starting structures
  4. Other — Flexible option for everything else
Best practice: Use "Other" unless you have a specific need.
Creating Your First Project
Project creation panel (name + design system + wireframe/high fidelity)
Steps:
  1. Choose your option (recommended: Other)
  2. Enter project name
  3. Select design system (optional)
  4. Choose Wireframe (basic structure) or High Fidelity (polished design)
  5. Click Create
Inside A Project Canvas
Once created, you'll see a new workspace:
This is where real work happens. You can start from a simple prompt, upload screenshots, attach files, or import references (Figma/code/images).
Empty canvas with "Start with context"
Key insight: Claude performs significantly better when given context.
Section IV — Design Systems (Advanced Feature)
This is where things get powerful. Design Systems act as predefined rules for your visuals. Instead of repeating instructions, you define them once.
Accessing Design Systems
Go to the Design Systems tab:
Design Systems tab highlighted
Creating A Design System
You'll be prompted to fill a setup form:
Design system input form
Here you can add brand description, design guidelines, fonts and colors, references, and codebases or files.
You don't need everything — but more input means better output consistency.
High-Level Strategy (Important)
A very effective approach: create a structured prompt or doc with your brand rules and paste it into the Notes section. Now Claude understands your entire design language.
Applying Design Systems
When starting a new project:
Selecting design system dropdown
You can choose your saved system. This ensures consistency across designs, faster generation, and less repetition.
What Happens After Setup
Once your system is ready, you'll see:
Design system ready / publish + default toggle
Options include publishing the system, setting it as default, and managing design files.
Two Core Workflows
Claude Design gives you two ways to work:
  1. New Project — Start fresh every time
  2. Design Systems — Reuse structured instructions
Professionals will mostly use systems.
Section V — Real Usage Flow
Inside a project, you simply write prompts like:
"Create a clean fintech dashboard with dark theme, card-based layout, and subtle gradients"
Claude will generate the design, show it on canvas, and let you iterate instantly.
Example Type Of Outputs
Example design output / project preview
You can build UI cards, landing sections, brand visuals, and presentations.
Usage Limits (Important Detail)
Claude Design operates on separate usage limits with a weekly reset system and plan-based access. It does NOT affect normal Claude chat usage.
Pro Tips (From Real Usage)
Be specific with prompts. Always provide context when possible. Use Design Systems for repeat work. Iterate instead of restarting. Use feedback controls (approve/adjust).
Final Take
Most people are still designing like it's 2022 — dragging elements, fixing spacing, adjusting layouts manually. But the shift is already happening: prompt-driven design, AI-assisted iteration, instant visual generation.
Claude Design isn't just faster. It fundamentally changes how design is done.
If you want a next level version, this can be turned into a viral thread, a carousel with hooks and slides, or a script for reels. Just say the word.
